title: One monotone colour curve fits 22 LCO visits of the 2020 ASASSN-14ko flare within stated error boxes
abstract: We test whether the rise and decline of one resolved ASASSN-14ko optical flare require different colours at the same brightness. A quadratic g-to-i flux relation prefers separate branches by Delta chi-square 25.12 with a 1 percent independent error floor. The rise is 167 +/- 32 microJy fainter in i at fixed g. However, an exact error-box test admits one nondecreasing relation through all 22 retained visits, without a site offset. It needs at most 1.384 error units per coordinate with a 1 percent floor, or 0.822 with a 2 percent floor. A concrete curve proves feasibility. A colour loop is therefore not required by this broader model class. We supply code, aggregate results, two figures, input hashes, simulations and a verified retrieval recipe. The source flux records remain external. This test uses one flare and prescribed independent errors. It allows arbitrary colour-curve slopes. It does not prove an instantaneous response, identify pericentre, or explain the period stall.

display.caption: One common monotone colour curve fits all 22 visits inside 0.822-error boxes when a 2 percent independent floor is included. No site offset is used.
A quadratic colour relation prefers separate rise and decline branches. Its rejection does not reject the flexible monotone class.
